calls.reason: The packet does not show the failed-adoption antecedent or a market turn. Census data shows uneven but growing adoption, and Amazon's 14,000 cuts were attributed to restructuring at a company it said was performing well.
OpenAI shut Sora down in 2026, but no reason was given beyond freeing up resources. Meanwhile Google's Veo and Flow kept running with over 275 million videos, so the category-wide claim is mixed.

A peer-reviewed PNAS Nexus study with comparison platforms found Stack Overflow activity fell 25% within six months of ChatGPT, with no drop in quality. A second study confirms the decline, though Reddit was unaffected.

There is no causal measure of content produced because of licensing deals. The Tow Center describes deals that paid for archives, while the Axios deal funded four new newsrooms, but it postdates the post and bundles licensing with expansion money.

The evidence from the time is mixed. Epoch projected data scarcity, phi-1 showed synthetic data works at small scale, and Klarna's $40M figure was a forecast, not realized profit. None of it settles either half of the claim.

The antecedent of a demand shortfall is not established. Microsoft reports demand still exceeding capacity, and Amazon cites strong demand. Investors pushed back on capex for Amazon and Microsoft but gave Google a pass.
